rules.name: SEEKING A PATH TOWARDS HEALING
rules.text: After playing cards each Spirit Phase: Claim a Healing Marker (Element Marker) matching whichever of [Water] or [Animal] you have more of. ( You break ties. ) You may then Claim a Healing Card if you meet its requirements. ( You can claim your first Healing Card on Turn 3. ) Then Destroy 1 [Presence] or Forget a Power Card ( unless a Healing Card just removed this rule ).
rules.turn:
-- "After playing cards each Spirit Phase:"
after-play-cards, spirit:special S seeking-a-path, ~seeking S
seeking S
  ~>claim-marker S
  ~>maybe-claim-healing S
  ~pay-the-cost S

-- "Claim a Healing Marker (Element Marker) matching whichever of Water or
--  Animal you have more of. (You break ties.)"
#acc markers : spirit element @sum
spirit S, element E / markers S E 0
healing-marker S E / markers S E 1
claim-marker S, elements S water W, elements S animal A, gt W A, +healing-marker S water
claim-marker S, elements S water W, elements S animal A, lt W A, +healing-marker S animal
claim-marker S, elements S water W, elements S animal A, ge W A, le W A
  ?[rng] E
  !(healing-element E)
  ~tie-break S E
tie-break S C, is C E, +healing-marker S E
setup, +healing-element water, +healing-element animal

-- "You may then Claim a Healing Card if you meet its requirements. (You can
--  claim your first Healing Card on Turn 3.)"
-- (turn 3 = two turns already done; the card and its requirement are invented:
--  "serene-waters: 2 Water Healing Markers; removes Seeking a Path")
maybe-claim-healing S, turns-done N, ge N 2, healing-card H, healing:water H Need, markers S water M, ge M Need
  ?[rng] R
  !(may R)
  ~healing-ask S H R N
-- (healing-ask carries the turn number N: `>healing-ask` alone would also
--  match the ask of an earlier turn)
seeking S, turns-done N, >healing-ask S H R N, is R yes
  +claimed S H
  ^healing-claimed S H
-- a claimed card that removes this rule: from now on the rule is gone ...
seeking S, turns-done N, >healing-ask S H R N, is R yes, healing:removes-rule H
  +rule-removed S seeking-a-path
turn, rule-removed S seeking-a-path, { seeking S => }

-- "Then Destroy 1 Presence or Forget a Power Card"
#acc wounded-option : spirit e
pay-the-cost S, presence-of S P, at P L, land L / wounded-option S P
pay-the-cost S, power:owner P S, at P hand / wounded-option S P
pay-the-cost S
  ?[rng] O
  !(wounded-option S O)
  ~cost-choice S O
cost-choice S O, is O P, presence-of S P, ~destroy-presence O
cost-choice S O, is O P, power:owner P S, ~forget S P
-- "(unless a Healing Card just removed this rule)"
seeking S, turns-done N, >healing-ask S H R N, is R yes, healing:removes-rule H, { pay-the-cost S => }
rules.evidence: 3 turns, seed 7: seeking-on-turn 0, healing-marker wounded water, paid-cost 0 w1; seeking-on-turn 1, healing-marker wounded animal, paid-cost 1 tide; seeking-on-turn 2, healing-marker wounded water, claimed wounded serene-waters (no cost paid). Seed 2 declines the card on turn 3 and pays (paid-cost 2 w3). A 4-turn run has no seeking on turn 4 after the claim (rule removed).
rules.notes: The three steps are a sequenced episode (`seeking S` -> claim-marker; maybe-claim-healing; pay-the-cost). The tie-break is a choice between Water and Animal. 'Unless a Healing Card just removed this rule' is a scoped exception on pay-the-cost; removing the rule for later turns is a fact plus an exception on `seeking`. The Healing Card (serene-waters: 2 Water markers, removes the rule) is INVENTED, since the real Healing Cards weren't in the sources; the real cards' replacement rules are not modeled. Bugs hit along the way: `spirit-phase, >play-cards` re-fired for every previous turn, and `+rule-removed` asserted from a rule anchored on a forever-fact wasn't visible on the next turn.

base_ext: Multiple turns (each finished turn starts the next, counted by a `turns-done` @sum acc), a play-cards / after-play-cards step in the Spirit Phase, Power Cards with a location (hand/forgotten) and `forget`, a yes/no `may` domain. The played cards are a turn-scoped acc view (`#acc played`, `turn … / played …`): a `turn, ^played …` view now starts concurrently with the phases.
language_issues: `>p` matches ANY earlier p, including previous turns' episodes (`spirit-phase, >play-cards` fired once per earlier turn); workaround: an explicit `after-...` step, or key the episode by turn number (`>healing-ask S H R N` with `turns-done N`).

A fact asserted by a rule anchored on another forever-fact (`claimed S H, ..., +rule-removed ...`) floats and wasn't visible to the next turn's exception; assert it inside a bounded episode (the seeking step) instead.
core is single-turn; multi-turn needs a counter and a `game, >turn, ... ~turn` rule. core's `+ravaged X -> 1` (#agg, to top) then leaks, so turns 2+ never Ravage.
